content: Physical activity for individuals with diabetes should be progressively increased in terms of intensity, frequency, and/or duration. The goal is to achieve a minimum of 150 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise per week. For adults capable of running at a pace of approximately 6 miles per hour (9.7 km/h) for at least 25 minutes, engaging in shorter durations of vigorous-intensity exercise or interval training—totaling around 75 minutes per week—can also provide significant health benefits. Adults with diabetes are also advised to incorporate resistance training exercises into their routine. These exercises, which may include the use of free weights or resistance bands, should be performed 2 to 3 times per week on nonconsecutive days. While heavier resistance training can lead to improved blood glucose regulation and increased muscular strength, even low-intensity resistance exercises are beneficial. They can enhance muscle strength, improve balance, and support functional abilities in daily life.
